scope: Actual CMP102 localized variational quadratic/linearization dictionary versus the bare first-integral Gaussian. Selected historical source identities and participating-parent critical-Hessian calculation, unreviewed; no new paper/review or physical admission.

source_anchors.identity: Variational coordinates satisfy mixed-scale nonlinear averages and RD* A=0 in the Landau representation; later an original axial-gauge representative is recovered.

The action expansion is constant+<A,J>+1/2<A,Delta_pi A>+V0(A); replacing Delta by Delta_pi uses the stated Landau restriction. This is not an equality with a soft-gauge free precision on the entire integration space.
H minimizes a quadratic under the mixed average and Landau constraints, Lj eta Qj H=I on the corresponding data. The source linearizes with A=Aprime-H D(Aprime), where D begins at quadratic order.
The source expressly says there are many linearizing transformations and h=H is a convenient nonunique choice. It introduces pseudo-locality of functional derivatives, not exact finite support.
A Neumann series and exponential derivative bound are stated for the nonlinear map; the transformed action and mixed linear constraints retain H, D and the Landau condition.

nonidentifications: CMP102 H is a variational extension tied to its mixed-scale determining set and gauge; it is not CMP109 selected-interface h or the free reconstruction R_rec.
Do not transfer the bare selected-map finite-carrier incidence to H D merely because both maps linearize an average. The source offers pseudo-local kernels and their own scales/weights instead.
Do not identify the variational Landau quadratic with the bare soft-gauge Gaussian. Restriction/gauge integration, coordinate volume and constraint determinants require an actual correspondence.

Different right-inverse maps alone do NOT prove different constrained quadratic laws. The source itself permits different choices; critical cancellation must be checked before claiming an obstruction.

critical_hessian_check.premises: One SAME real action S, SAME smooth constraint F=0 and SAME critical point on a common admissible chart. Let L=DF(0) and dS(0)=lambda composed with L. Let T_h,T_H linearize the same constraint, both based at0 and tangent to identity; take b,c in ker L.
critical_hessian_check.identity: Differentiating F(T_i(tb+uc))=0 on the tangent slice gives L D2T_i[b,c]=-D2F[b,c]. Thus D2(S composed T_i)[b,c]=D2S[b,c]-lambda(D2F[b,c]), independent of the right inverse i.
critical_hessian_check.equivalent_cancellation: When normalized right inverses satisfy Lh=LH=I, L(H-h)=0; the critical linear/current functional annihilates (H-h)D2F. Dropping the current correction would erase this identity.
critical_hessian_check.what_it_reduces: The mere choice h versus H need not be added as an independent Gaussian-Hessian obstruction for one identical critical constrained problem. The actual source current/constraint term is the appropriate correction.
critical_hessian_check.what_it_does_not_reduce: The localized and global source problems have different determining constraints/backgrounds, possibly gauges and coordinate spaces. The premises are not established between them. Nonlinear remainders, Jacobians and original cutoff sets need not agree even when same-problem quadratic Hessians agree.

research_decision.rejected_shortcuts: Neither h=H by notation nor h differs from H therefore inequivalent physical Gaussian is adopted. No principal-conditioning identity follows from the inspected source statements.
research_decision.useful_comparison_target: Treat the source localized minimizer first as a BACKGROUND function. A genuine source comparison of global and localized critical backgrounds, followed by matched-frame finite-prototype estimates for their SAME bare Qfree, could provide an operator-localization estimate. This avoids demanding that a different variational H itself be the raw Gaussian conditional covariance.
research_decision.still_required: The actual determining-set change and common-coordinate/frame/gauge transport, quantitative background comparison kernel, original free cutoff and all Jacobian/normalizer/boundary factors. A derivative bound within one fixed constraint problem alone does not compare two different determining sets.
research_decision.next: Locate the source statement that compares minimal backgrounds for changed/localized determining data, with its exact metric, gauge return and domain hypotheses. Bind it to the original CMP119 construction before transporting Qfree; if only fixed-data derivatives are available, retain that narrower scope. No repeated abstract right-inverse/Gaussian lemma or new minor-paper/review route.
